push_channels.guide.trigger: View push channel application and integration guides
push_channels.guide.title: Push channel application and integration guides
push_channels.guide.intro: For each provider, complete account verification, app registration, Push enablement, and credential creation before entering the matching values in AppKernia. Secret fields are never displayed after saving.
push_channels.guide.provider.apns.summar: All iOS distributions use APNs. Token authentication with a .p8 key is recommended, and the APNs topic must exactly match the app Bundle ID.
push_channels.guide.provider.apns.step.1: Create an Explicit App ID in Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles with the exact Bundle ID used by the app.
push_channels.guide.provider.apns.step.2: Enable Push Notifications for the App ID and confirm the signing profile contains this capability.
push_channels.guide.provider.apns.step.3: An authorized team member creates a Key with APNs access, records its Key ID, and downloads the one-time .p8 file immediately.
push_channels.guide.provider.apns.step.4: Get the Team ID from Membership, enter the Bundle ID, environment, and private key, then run server preflight.
Team ID on the Apple Developer Membership page; it is also the issuer of the APNs JWT.
Key ID shown after creating the APNs Key. It must match the uploaded .p8 private key.
The Explicit App ID Bundle ID, used as apns-topic and required to match the installed app.
Use Sandbox for development; use Production for TestFlight and App Store production signing.
The original .p8 downloaded when the Key is created. Apple offers it once, so first store it in an approved secret manager.
push_channels.guide.provider.apns.note: Do not upload an APNs certificate in place of a .p8 key. Verify Team ID, Key ID, Bundle ID, and environment; sandbox and production device tokens cannot be mixed.
push_channels.guide.provider.fcm.summary: The Google Play Android build uses FCM HTTP v1. The server exchanges a service account credential for a short-lived OAuth 2.0 access token.
Create a Firebase project and Android app
Add an Android app in Firebase with the package name used by the android_google build.
Confirm Firebase Cloud Messaging API is enabled and record the Project ID from project settings.
Create a least-privilege service account, download its JSON key, and store and rotate it under your security policy.
Enter the project ID, package name, and complete service account JSON, then verify OAuth and FCM API access.
push_channels.guide.provider.fcm.field.p: Project ID from Firebase project settings; it must match project_id in the service account JSON.
Android package name registered in Firebase; it must match the Google build applicationId.
push_channels.guide.provider.fcm.field.s: Complete JSON key containing client_email and private_key, written only to encrypted server storage.
push_channels.guide.provider.fcm.note: Do not enter a legacy Server key or include the service account JSON in the client or repository. Run preflight to verify HTTP v1 access.
push_channels.guide.provider.huawei_andr: Huawei Android devices use HMS Push Kit. Register the package and signing fingerprint in AppGallery Connect and enable Push Kit.
Create an AGC project and app
Create an Android app in AppGallery Connect using the exact package name of the China build.
Add the release certificate SHA-256 fingerprint and data processing location, then download the updated agconnect-services.json.
Enable Push Kit under project APIs and obtain the Client ID and Client Secret from app information.
Enter app details and the client notification channel ID, then validate server authorization and app matching.
Client ID under AppGallery Connect project settings, General information, App information.
Android package registered in AGC; it must match the signed build.
Android Notification Channel ID created by the client, not an AGC credential; keep it aligned with app code.
Client Secret from app information, written only to the server.
A package, SHA-256 fingerprint, or Client ID/Secret from different apps causes authorization or delivery failures. Refresh client configuration before testing.
push_channels.guide.provider.honor.summa: HONOR Android Push requires app registration, signing verification, agreement acceptance, and Push enablement in HONOR Developer Services.
Create an Android app, enter the exact package and release certificate SHA-256 fingerprint, and accept required service agreements.
Enable Push for the app and apply for notification classifications that match actual use cases.
Get App ID, Client ID, and Client Secret from app information and protect the Secret.
Add the client notification channel ID and verify HONOR IAM and the server downlink API.
push_channels.guide.provider.honor.field: App ID assigned by HONOR Developer Services and used in the server send path.
Client ID used to obtain an access token from HONOR IAM.
Android package registered with HONOR and used by the China build.
Android Notification Channel ID created and used by the client.
Client Secret paired with Client ID, written only to the server.
push_channels.guide.provider.honor.note: Verify package and signing fingerprint against the production build. Apply classifications honestly; operations content must not use a system category.
push_channels.guide.provider.xiaomi.summ: Xiaomi Push uses different server hosts by app data region. AppId, AppKey, and AppSecret must belong to the same app and region.
push_channels.guide.provider.xiaomi.step: Create the app and enable Push
Create an app on the Xiaomi platform, register the China build package, and enable Push.
Use the data region chosen for the app: China, Singapore, Europe, India, or Russia.
Get AppId, AppKey, and AppSecret from Push configuration. Never mix values from different apps.
Enter package, region, and client notification channel ID, then verify the regional server API.
push_channels.guide.provider.xiaomi.fiel: AppId assigned to the app in the Xiaomi Push console.
AppKey paired with the AppId and used to identify the app on the client.
Android package registered with Xiaomi and used by the China build.
App data service region, which selects the server API host and should not be changed casually.
Notification channel ID created by the client for Android 8 and later.
AppSecret used by the server REST API, written only to the server.
push_channels.guide.provider.xiaomi.note: The wrong region causes authorization or token failures. China, Singapore, Europe, India, and Russia must use their officially listed API hosts.
push_channels.guide.provider.oppo.summar: OPPO PUSH generally requires an enterprise developer account and app review. Obtain AppKey and MasterSecret after enablement.
push_channels.guide.provider.oppo.step.1: Verify the enterprise and create an app
Complete enterprise verification and create an Android app with the production package name.
push_channels.guide.provider.oppo.step.2: Submit the required app and Push service application in the console and wait for approval.
push_channels.guide.provider.oppo.step.3: Get AppKey and MasterSecret from Push settings; the notification channel is created and synchronized by the client.
push_channels.guide.provider.oppo.step.4: Enter package, credentials, and notification channel ID, then validate authorization and service status.
AppKey in the OPPO Push app configuration.
Android package registered with OPPO and used by the China build.
Notification Channel ID created by the client and synchronized for OPPO Push.
MasterSecret used for server authorization, written only to the server.
push_channels.guide.provider.oppo.note: Never put MasterSecret in the app. Before production testing, confirm both app review and PUSH entitlement are approved and the client creates the channel.
push_channels.guide.provider.vivo.summar: vivo Push requires app review and service enablement. System and operations messages use different classification values and provider-approved categories.
push_channels.guide.provider.vivo.step.1: Create an app on vivo Developer Platform, enter the production package, and complete required review.
push_channels.guide.provider.vivo.step.2: Enable message Push and initialize the SDK only after user consent under the current privacy requirements.
push_channels.guide.provider.vivo.step.3: Get AppID, AppKey, and AppSecret, then apply for system or operations categories that match real use cases.
push_channels.guide.provider.vivo.step.4: Enter provider-approved uppercase category codes and validate authorization and classification entitlement.
AppID assigned by the vivo Push console.
AppKey paired with AppID and used to identify the app on the client.
Android package registered with vivo and used by the China build.
Provider-approved uppercase system category, only for a qualifying use case; sent with classification=1.
Provider-approved uppercase operations category, such as an approved NEWS or CONTENT; sent with classification=0.
AppSecret used for vivo server authorization, written only to the server.
push_channels.guide.provider.vivo.note: Never guess category values. Use the current console approval, and never classify operations content as system messages to bypass quota or opt-out.
push_channels.guide.provider.meizu.summa: Meizu Flyme Push requires developer verification and app creation before obtaining client identifiers and a server secret.
Register and complete developer verification on Flyme Open Platform.
Create an app under Message Push using the exact package name of the China build.
Get AppId, AppKey, and the server-only AppSecret from the console.
Use the official SDK to obtain PushId, then enter server settings and run preflight.
push_channels.guide.provider.meizu.field: AppId assigned in the Flyme Push console.
AppKey used to initialize the Meizu client SDK.
Android package registered with Flyme and used by the China build.
AppSecret used to call the Flyme Push server API, written only to the server.
push_channels.guide.provider.meizu.note: Never include AppSecret in the client. Recheck the platform app and client PushId after package or signing changes.
push_channels.guide.provider.harmony.sum: HarmonyOS NEXT uses Push Kit and short-lived service account JWTs. Apply message categories by project and actual use case.
push_channels.guide.provider.harmony.ste: Create a HarmonyOS app in AppGallery Connect and confirm Project ID, Client ID, and Bundle Name.
Enable Push Kit and apply self-classified message entitlements for service and operations use cases.
Create a service account with Push access in API Console and download the JSON credential used for short-lived JWTs.
Enter app identifiers, approved categories, and complete JSON, then validate service account project access.
push_channels.guide.provider.harmony.fie: Project ID of the HarmonyOS app in AppGallery Connect.
Client ID assigned to the HarmonyOS app.
HarmonyOS Bundle Name; it must match the signed app.
Provider-approved uppercase self-classified service category matching the actual service scenario.
Provider-approved uppercase operations category, commonly an approved MARKETING value; use the console result.
Complete service account JSON with Push access, written only to the server and used for short-lived JWTs.
push_channels.guide.provider.harmony.not: Use current Push Kit console entitlements and quotas. Never place service account JSON in the HAP, logs, or repository.
